subject.title: [Bug] Docker sandbox container name collision across multiple instances on same host

question: Should OpenClaw accept workspace-scoped non-shared sandbox runtime identity, including the documented one-time runtime reset, as the fix for this cross-instance Docker sandbox collision?
rationale: The code defect is source-reproducible, but the fix changes sandbox identity, registry/recreate semantics, and upgrade behavior for an isolation boundary, which needs maintainer security and compatibility intent.

options.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
options.body: Review and land the active workspace-scoped fix after explicitly accepting the one-time non-shared runtime reset and cleanup behavior.

options.title: Require an upgrade migration
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a doctor or migration path if preserving old non-shared runtime state is required.

options.title: Redesign backend-specific policy
options.body: Pause the current PR if Docker, browser, SSH, and skills workspace identity should not move together under one scope-key contract.

recommendation.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
recommendation.body: Review and land the active workspace-scoped fix after explicitly accepting the one-time non-shared runtime reset and cleanup behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows repeated sandbox security, cleanup, docs, and Docker/browser work in the affected owner boundary.
